citation.authors: Dennis AC, DeAngelis R, Hargrove TW, Pearson JA
citation.journal: Journal of Health and Social Behavior

cited_by.title: Colourism, skin tone and mental health

record.finding: Black adults who perceived themselves as dark-skinned had a lower sense of mattering and shorter telomeres than those who perceived their skin lighter, regardless of interviewer-rated skin tone.
record.note: One city; telomeres are a research biomarker, not a diagnosis.
